title: You Probably Forget How Cheap Memory Used To Be – And Is Not So Now
gist: Reporting from Hot Chips 2026 and analyst Jim Handy's memory tutorial, the piece argues DRAM/HBM/NAND are in a demand-shock supercycle — spot prices up roughly 7x — driven by hyperscaler GenAI and agentic-AI buildouts, with GPU components sold out through 2027, Nvidia signaling a 15% NVL72 price hike, and Broadcom emerging as the third-largest HBM buyer; the structural escape route is smarter memory (PIM, compute on HBM base dies, flash-based KV-cache tiers).

insights.claim: DRAM, HBM, and NAND flash prices are in a stratospheric run because a massive AI demand shock is colliding head-on with a dearth of supply, with spot-market prices up roughly seven times.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A ~7x spot move signals a memory supercycle; contracted buyers and memory makers' margins are the direct beneficiaries — system OEMs and AI startups bear the cost.
insights.quote: you've got these prices that have gone up about seven times on the spot market, which is not a very good indicator, but it's an easy one to measure
insights.locator: It's all made on the same manufacturing line

insights.claim: Memory and flash shortages and price strength are expected to persist through at least 2030, based on prognostications that see the GenAI boom growing until then.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A multi-year shortage window through 2030 supports a long-duration overweight in memory makers rather than treating this as a one- or two-year cyclical spike.
insights.quote: all the prognostications I have seen see it growing through 2030 at the least and shortages continuing until that time at least
insights.locator: Look at that memory and flash crash

insights.claim: The price inflation extends across the entire storage hierarchy down to hard disk drives, which hyperscalers are consuming in volume as near-cold storage, so the big five memory and flash makers are posting outsized revenues.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The AI storage bid is broader than HBM — HDD and commodity NAND/DRAM vendors also capture pricing power; watch the whole storage stack, not just HBM names.
insights.quote: prices for all kinds of storage, all the way back to hard disk drives, which are largely consumed by the tech titans as nearly cold storage, are skyrocketing
insights.locator: Because of this demand from the hyperscalers

insights.claim: The 2022-2023 memory and flash revenue crash occurred ironically just as GenAI was getting started, illustrating how fast the cycle flipped from glut to shortage.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Memory remains violently cyclical — the same speed of reversal applies on the way down if AI capex decelerates; size positions with that asymmetry in mind.
insights.quote: Look at that memory and flash crash back in late 2022 and in early 2023, when GenAI ironically was just getting started.
insights.locator: Look at that memory and flash crash

insights.claim: Because flash, DRAM, and HBM are made on the same manufacturing lines, HBM demand is pulling DDR and NAND prices up with it — the shortage propagates across all memory types via shared fab capacity.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM capacity absorption is the transmission mechanism for the entire memory complex — track HBM wafer allocation to forecast commodity DRAM/NAND pricing.
insights.quote: It's all made on the same manufacturing line
insights.locator: It's all made on the same manufacturing line

insights.claim: In a shortage, memory's commodity nature inverts the power dynamic: manufacturers abandon long-standing customers for whoever pays the higher price, since interchangeability cuts both ways.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Buyers without volume commitments or balance-sheet firepower get rationed out first — favor players with locked supply deals; expect startups to be squeezed.
insights.quote: But it also means that the manufacturers, when there's a shortage, then they don't care about you.
insights.locator: It's all made on the same manufacturing line

insights.claim: Spot memory pricing is only a rough average; system and chip makers integrating HBM or LPDDR5X on-package strike individual deals with their own price and volume commitments, some beating spot and some doing worse.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Headline spot prices overstate or understate actual cost exposure per company — dig into contract structures before extrapolating margin impact from spot moves.
insights.locator: Spot pricing is a kind of average

insights.claim: Broadcom has become the third-largest HBM buyer behind Nvidia and AMD via its custom XPU business, buying capacity on behalf of AI hardware startups that could not otherwise secure etching and packaging.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Broadcom's HBM buying power makes it the effective gatekeeper for custom-silicon challengers to Nvidia — its HBM allocation is a leading indicator of XPU competition.
insights.quote: Broadcom is now the third largest buyer of HBM memory, behind Nvidia and AMD
insights.locator: For instance, as the highest volume buyer

insights.claim: With GPU components sold out for 2026 and allocations essentially done through end-2027, Nvidia is warning buyers of Grace-Blackwell and Vera-Rubin NVL72 systems of a 15 percent price increase next year — and the author is surprised the hike is not larger.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia can pass memory inflation through to ODMs/OEMs and end buyers; AI compute cost-per-system is rising, pressuring downstream AI economics while protecting Nvidia margins.
insights.quote: there is a 15 percent price increase coming, according to reports in Bloomberg
insights.locator: Hence, with all of the GPU components

insights.claim: Nvidia's revenue growth is capped by the HBM supply it can secure, and it must deliberately leave HBM capacity for competitors to avoid antitrust exposure — historically an 85 percent share threshold at the DOJ, though now subject to President Trump's discretion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: HBM supply, not demand, is Nvidia's growth governor — and antitrust/political risk constrains how aggressively it can corner memory; watch competitor HBM access as a policy barometer.
insights.quote: Nvidia’s business can only grow as fast as the HBM memory it can get, the same as every other GPU and XPU maker.

insights.claim: AI infrastructure capex is dominated by four US hyperscalers — AWS, Google, Microsoft Azure, and Meta — against which Alibaba, the biggest Chinese hyperscaler, barely registers.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The memory demand shock is concentrated in four US buyers — their capex guidance is the single best forward indicator for the memory cycle; China capex is not the marginal driver.
insights.quote: Alibaba, the biggest of the Chinese hyperscalers that also has a cloud business, barely registers against the vast spending by the big four tech titans in the United States
insights.locator: What I find interesting in this chart

insights.claim: Apple's AI capital investment in 2026 is smaller than in the prior five years, and its capex-light approach — selling AI at a profit without building the infrastructure — is framed as an enviable position.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Apple is the anti-consensus AI capex play: capturing AI value without the depreciation burden the hyperscalers are loading on; contrast against soaring hyperscaler capex intensity.
insights.quote: if you can sell AI at a profit and not have to do the capital investing, then go, be, do
insights.locator: What I find interesting in this chart

insights.claim: Agentic AI is creating a distinct demand leg for CPUs plus DRAM and flash, because agents need sandboxes to run masses of generated (and possibly low-quality) Python and other code.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Agentic AI extends the AI infrastructure bid beyond GPUs into general-purpose CPU and commodity memory demand — a tailwind for server CPU and DRAM vendors, not just accelerator names.
insights.locator: The main culprit is the hyperscalers

themes.theme: Smart memory as the memory-wall escape

insights.claim: The industry's structural response to memory scarcity is moving compute toward the data: externalized flash-based, DPU-driven storage tiers for KV caches, compute added to HBM base dies, and Processing In Memory.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: PIM, smart HBM base dies, and KV-cache offload tiers are the architectural hedge against permanent memory inflation — watch vendors commercializing these for asymmetric upside.
insights.locator: What the industry needs to do

insights.claim: Bandwidth requirements of a communications channel fall as intelligence at either endpoint rises — smarter memory chips that execute operations locally (e.g., an in-memory sort returning one byte) will cut processor-memory traffic and route around the memory wall.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: This framework implies the winning response to HBM scarcity is reducing bandwidth need, not just adding bandwidth — favors compute-in-memory architectures over brute-force HBM stacking.
insights.quote: we are probably headed towards having smarter memory chips that will end up reducing the amount of traffic it needs to go to the processor

insights.claim: AI will permeate to every endpoint — down to microcontrollers and inside communication channels — to the point of becoming invisible, driven by a new willingness to transplant working AI techniques into new domains.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals a coming edge/embedded-AI diffusion wave beyond datacenters — a long-tail demand vector for low-power silicon and embedded memory.
insights.quote: I'm expecting to see AI used at all of the endpoints. I'm expecting to see it in the communication channel, and it will get to the point where it's invisible.
